headline: Cloudflare blocked 18.2M DDoS attacks in Q3 2026, with 96% ending in under ten minutes
summary: Cloudflare's Q3 2026 report shows a 208% surge in short-burst DDoS attacks, while hyper-volumetric attacks dropped 69%, shifting the defensive challenge.
details: Cloudflare mitigated 18.2 million network-layer DDoS attacks and 14.4 trillion HTTP DDoS requests in Q3 2026. This translates to roughly 8,226 network-layer attacks per hour, or one attack every 0.44 seconds. Mitigated traffic reached 272.6 PB at the network layer.

The company attributes its ability to absorb this volume to automation, with unmetered DDoS protection across 330+ cities and 500 Tbps of capacity. These systems detect and mitigate attacks without human intervention, which is crucial given the rapid attack cadence.
Short-burst, mid-range attacks defined the quarter, increasing 208% compared to Q3 2025. The report indicates that 96% of network-layer attacks lasted under ten minutes, and 98% were under 1 Gbps.

The top target industries for these short-duration attacks included computer software (21.1%), gambling and casinos (14.4%), information technology and services (14%), and telecommunications (12.4%). These sectors are particularly exposed due to their financial nature and uptime requirements.

Conversely, hyper-volumetric attacks exceeding 1 Tbps fell sharply by nearly 69%, from 805 in Q2 to 251 in Q3. This decline may be linked to law enforcement actions against major IoT botnets like Aisuru, KimWolf, JackSkid, and Mossad earlier in 2026.

Attack tactics also rotated, with CLDAP floods collapsing by 99.5% to 0.05% of attacks. Attackers shifted to other connectionless protocols, with DNS amplification rising 215% to 3.43% and other UDP floods climbing from 14.06% to 31.31%.

Both DNS amplification and UDP floods utilize similar reflection-and-amplification patterns, making the switch easy for attackers. Organizations can mitigate this by closing open resolvers that answer recursion from the open internet.

headline: Paris robotaxi consortium launched, but no vehicles run today
summary: Métropole du Grand Paris, Bolt, and Stellantis form a consortium for autonomous vehicles, targeting commercial service by 2030.
details: The Métropole du Grand Paris, alongside mobility company Bolt and automotive giant Stellantis, has announced the Greater Paris Autonomous Driving Living Lab. This consortium aims to operate autonomous vehicles within the Paris metropolitan area, with testing slated to begin in 2028.

The project outlines a phased approach, starting with testing in up to five municipalities. A subsequent phase would explore expansion to approximately thirty more areas, with the ultimate goal of launching commercial services by 2030. All operations are contingent on receiving necessary authorizations.

Stellantis will provide vehicles built on its 'L4-Ready' platforms, while Bolt, through its subsidiary Bolt Autonomous Driving Solutions, will lead service integration and deployment. This includes organizing the overall service, connecting vehicles, autonomous driving technology, and the customer-facing digital platform.

Key details such as the specific municipalities involved, the size of the fleet, and the total investment remain undisclosed. Notably, the crucial role of operating the vehicles day-to-day – including maintenance, charging, and dispatch – has not yet been assigned to any specific party within the consortium.

Unlike previous European projects, the public authority, Métropole du Grand Paris, is an active partner, coordinating with municipalities and identifying routes. This suggests the design of service areas and their rollout order will be determined collaboratively between the authority and the platform.
